memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'A foreigner residing among you is also to celebrate the Lord's Passover in accordance with its rules and regulations. You must have the same regulations for both the foreigner and the native-born.'" - Num 9:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God adds something wonderful: the foreigner living among Israel could also keep the Passover. The same rules applied to the outsider as to the native-born. There was room at God's table for those who were not born into Israel but who came to trust and worship the true God.

This is a beautiful glimpse of God's heart for all peoples, shining out even in the Old Testament. God's love was never meant to be locked up within one nation only. From the very beginning, His plan was to draw people from every background into relationship with Him. The stranger who came in faith was welcomed on equal terms.

How this must have encouraged any foreigner among the Israelites — to know they were not second-class, not kept at a distance, but invited to share fully in the worship of God. The same grace, the same feast, the same welcome.

This points forward to the great truth of the gospel. In Christ, the dividing wall between insiders and outsiders has come down. Paul writes that Gentiles who were once "foreigners" are now "fellow citizens with God's people and also members of his household" (Eph 2:19). The invitation goes out to all.

Whoever you are, whatever your background, there is room at God's table for you in Christ. And as those who have been welcomed, we are called to welcome others too. Let no one feel like an outsider where God offers a full and equal welcome.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you ever feel like an outsider to God's family?
- How does it move you that God welcomes all who come in faith?
- How can you help others feel welcomed at God's table?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that in Christ there is room at Your table for all who come. Help me to rest in Your welcome, and to welcome others as You have welcomed me. Amen.
